chunks: From him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr and Safwan, from Isḥaq ibn ʿAmmār, who said:

I said to Abū Ibrāhīm (peace be upon him): 'It has reached us from your father that if a man marries a woman during her waiting period (ʿiddah), she is not permissible to him ever.' He said: 'This is if he was knowledgeable. But if he was ignorant, he divorces her, she completes her waiting period, and then he marries her with a new marriage contract.'
ai.seo_question: What is the difference between marrying during ʿiddah knowingly versus unknowingly in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Istibsar highlights the juristic distinction between knowledge (ʿilm) and ignorance (jahal) in determining the permanence of a marriage contract during the ʿiddah. While the general principle often cited is that such a marriage is invalid forever, this hadith clarifies that for the ignorant party, the defect is curable through a fresh divorce and a new contract (nikah jadid), reflecting the Shia emphasis on procedural rectification over absolute nullification in cases of excusable error.
